records.student_text: Which velocity vector correctly represents motion down at 2 m/s if the reference arrow for 2 m/s has the stated scale?
records.student_html:
Which velocity vector correctly represents motion down at 2 m/s if the reference arrow for 2 m/s has the stated scale?

  1. a dot with no direction
  2. an arrow pointing down with the correct scaled length
  3. an arrow pointing opposite down with the correct length
  4. an arrow pointing down with zero length
Draw the requested vector(s) here.
choices: a dot with no direction
an arrow pointing down with the correct scaled length
an arrow pointing opposite down with the correct length
an arrow pointing down with zero length
records.answer: An arrow pointing down with a length representing 2 m/s.
records.solution_text: A velocity vector must encode both magnitude and direction: orientation gives direction and length represents speed.
records.solution_html: A velocity vector must encode both magnitude and direction: orientation gives direction and length represents speed.

records.student_text: A robot moves at a constant speed of 4 m/s. At first it moves east, then it turns and moves north while keeping the same speed. Compare its speed and velocity before and after the turn.
records.student_html:
A robot moves at a constant speed of 4 m/s. At first it moves east, then it turns and moves north while keeping the same speed. Compare its speed and velocity before and after the turn.

  1. The speed remains 4 m/s, but the velocity changes because its direction changes from east to north.
  2. Both speed and velocity remain constant because the speedometer value is unchanged.
  3. The speed changes but the velocity does not.
  4. Velocity has no direction, so only position changes.
choices: The speed remains 4 m/s, but the velocity changes because its direction changes from east to north.
Both speed and velocity remain constant because the speedometer value is unchanged.
The speed changes but the velocity does not.
Velocity has no direction, so only position changes.
records.answer: The speed remains 4 m/s, but the velocity changes because its direction changes from east to north.
records.solution_text: Velocity includes magnitude and direction. A direction change changes velocity even when the speed stays constant.
records.solution_html: Velocity includes magnitude and direction. A direction change changes velocity even when the speed stays constant.

records.student_text: Vector A is 4 cm long and points east. Vector B is 4 cm long and points north. Determine whether the object’s velocity changed and explain what feature of the vectors supports your answer.
records.student_html:
Vector A is 4 cm long and points east. Vector B is 4 cm long and points north. Determine whether the object’s velocity changed and explain what feature of the vectors supports your answer.

  1. No; equal arrow lengths guarantee equal velocity.
  2. No; direction is not part of velocity.
  3. Yes only if the arrow lengths also change.
  4. Yes. The speed magnitude can be the same, but the direction changes from east to north, so velocity changes.
Show your reasoning here.
choices: No; equal arrow lengths guarantee equal velocity.
No; direction is not part of velocity.
Yes only if the arrow lengths also change.
Yes. The speed magnitude can be the same, but the direction changes from east to north, so velocity changes.
records.answer: Yes. The speed magnitude can be the same, but the direction changes from east to north, so velocity changes.
records.solution_text: Velocity vectors are equal only when both magnitude and direction are equal. Changing direction changes velocity.
records.solution_html: Velocity vectors are equal only when both magnitude and direction are equal. Changing direction changes velocity.

records.student_text: A position–time graph is shown. Write a motion description consistent with the graph, then identify one common incorrect interpretation and correct it.
records.student_html:
A position–time graph is shown. Write a motion description consistent with the graph, then identify one common incorrect interpretation and correct it.

  1. The object is climbing a physical hill because the line rises.
  2. The object is accelerating because position increases.
  3. The object is at rest because the line is straight.
  4. The object moves in the positive direction at constant velocity 2 m/s. The graph height represents position, not physical height above the ground.
choices: The object is climbing a physical hill because the line rises.
The object is accelerating because position increases.
The object is at rest because the line is straight.
The object moves in the positive direction at constant velocity 2 m/s. The graph height represents position, not physical height above the ground.
records.answer: The object moves in the positive direction at constant velocity 2 m/s. The graph height represents position, not physical height above the ground.
records.solution_text: The straight-line position–time graph has constant slope 2 m/s, so velocity is constant. The vertical axis is position, so it should not be read as a picture of a hill.
records.solution_html: The straight-line position–time graph has constant slope 2 m/s, so velocity is constant. The vertical axis is position, so it should not be read as a picture of a hill.
